ranking_policy: Coverage-complete planning scan for LibWit, a book composer that must produce one coherent book covering EVERY item of an author-supplied requirement set — each item exactly once, none missing — where the evidence corpus behind the book can reach millions of documents while the planner's context is a few tens of kilobytes. Rank papers by how directly their mechanism would fix a COVERAGE-GUARANTEE or CORPUS-SCALE-PLANNING failure in such a system: plan-time completeness contracts and plan verification, item-set/set-cover/submodular selection of representatives, hierarchical summarisation and tree-reduction over corpora larger than any context window, plan-then-write long-form generation with section-level evidence binding, cross-section deduplication and novelty control, stable item identity across re-planning, and measurable coverage/recall of a requirement set. Papers that build or audit the plan/coverage machinery itself rank above papers whose coverage is a side experiment; papers matched by multiple topics rank above single-topic matches; break ties by citation signal and recency.
